title: The longest and the shortest

segments.voice: Yesterday, sajdah: the verses where the reciter goes down to the ground. Your line was bow where it bows. Did you let yourself be small in front of something bigger? Day three hundred twenty-five.

Two surahs. One is so long that reciting it aloud takes well over an hour, and it fills nearly fifty pages of a standard mushaf. The other you can say in the time it takes to tie your shoes, and a child can learn it in an afternoon. They sit near opposite ends of the book, and Muslims hold that both are equally the word of God. Today: the longest and the shortest.
screen: `WELL OVER AN HOUR.` → `THE TIME IT TAKES TO TIE YOUR SHOES.` → `BOTH EQUALLY THE QUR'AN.`

segments.voice: The longest is al-Baqarah, the Cow, Surah 2, with two hundred and eighty-six verses. It's named for a story inside it: Musa telling his people to sacrifice a cow, and their endless questions stalling the command. Al-Baqarah holds almost everything: the story of Adam, the turning of the prayer toward Mecca, fasting in Ramadan, pilgrimage, charity, marriage and divorce, debts. It holds the longest single verse in the Qur'an, about writing down a loan, and Ayat al-Kursi, the Throne Verse. And near its end, in Pickthall's words: "Allah tasketh not a soul beyond its scope." The Prophet ﷺ said, in a hadith in Muslim: don't make your houses into graveyards; Satan flees from a house in which Surah al-Baqarah is recited. The shortest is al-Kawthar, Surah 108: three verses, about ten Arabic words. You learned it in camp four. "Lo! We have given thee Abundance;" then: so pray to your Lord, and sacrifice. Then: the one who hates you is the one cut off. Reports say it came at a hard time, when the Prophet's sons had died young and an enemy mocked him as cut off, a man with no line. Three verses to answer a grief. Here's what's worth noticing. A surah's weight isn't its length. Al-Kawthar is complete, a whole surah, just as al-Baqarah is. The Qur'an's challenge to bring a surah like it applies to the short ones as much as the long. And both open with the same bismillah. Long and short: some days you need the whole house, and some days one room is enough.
screen: `AL-BAQARAH: 286 VERSES` · `A HOUSE WHERE IT'S RECITED` · `AL-KAWTHAR: THREE VERSES` · `WEIGHT ISN'T LENGTH`

segments.voice: Here's the practice: read al-Kawthar once more. If you know it, say it now, slowly, all three verses, bismillah first. If you don't, remember it in English: abundance; pray and sacrifice; the one cut off. Then sit with the first verse only. Abundance. What have you been given that you forget to count? Let one thing come to mind, and stay with it. If another comes, let it join the first. The bell holds the time.
The longest and the shortest. Al-Baqarah, two hundred and eighty-six verses; al-Kawthar, three. Each one a whole surah. Today's word.
screen: `THE LONGEST AND THE SHORTEST — today's word`.

segments.voice: Your line: long and short. Today, give one thing the long version, a real conversation, a slow meal, and let another be short and complete: a three-word thank you. Day three hundred twenty-five.

howItsDone: Many Muslims recite al-Baqarah at home, in portions or in full, because of the hadith about the house where it is recited, and al-Kawthar is among the short surahs often recited in the daily prayers.

fork.reveal: three verses: abundance given, pray and sacrifice, and the one who hates you is the one cut off.

original.note: Arabic: abundance, overflowing good. hadith also name al-Kawthar as a river in paradise.

trapdoor: what you thought: the first surah is the longest and the last is the shortest.
what it means: al-Baqarah, the second, is the longest; al-Kawthar, the 108th, is the shortest, with three verses.
what a scholar hears: 2:282, the debt verse, is the longest ayah, and many scholars say the challenge to bring a surah like it reaches even al-Kawthar.
